description: A three-input logic gate you define yourself: one button per row of the truth table sets what the output does for that combination of A, B and C.

params.text: Sets the output for one row of the truth table. Lit, the Q output is 10V while A, B and C are at the levels printed on that row; unlit, it is 0V.

inputs.text: The first input, worth four when the three inputs are read as the row number.
The second input, worth two when the three inputs are read as the row number.
The third input, worth one when the three inputs are read as the row number.

outputs.text: 10V while the button on the row the inputs have selected is lit, 0V while it is unlit.
The inverse of Q: 10V while the button on the selected row is unlit.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
Every button comes up unlit, which leaves Q at 0V whatever the inputs do; press the button on each row that is to give a high output before patching anything.

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
